item.claim: More patients discontinued because of adverse events on drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports more patients with treatment-emergent adverse events leading to discontinuation on Drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).

item.claim: At week 26, drug R reduced HbA1c by 0.94% compared with 0.28% on placebo (difference -0.66%, p < 0.001).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The week 26 row reports the claimed HbA1c changes, treatment difference, and p-value.

item.claim: Systolic blood pressure fell numerically more with drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant (p = 0.247).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows a numerically larger fall with Drug R than placebo and a non-significant difference (p = 0.247).

item.claim: Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in the two groups (7.0% and 6.4%).
item.label: supported

result.quote:
Category | Drug R 10 mg (N=300) n (%) | Placebo (N=298) n (%)
Serious TEAE | 21 (7.0) | 19 (6.4)
result.reason: The table reports serious treatment-emergent adverse events in 7.0% of the Drug R group and 6.4% of the placebo group, consistent with the claim’s characterization of the rates as similar.

item.claim: Body weight decreased by 2.1 kg with drug R and 0.6 kg with placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The week 26 table reports body-weight changes of −2.1 kg with Drug R and −0.6 kg with placebo.

item.claim: Nearly 40% of drug R patients reached HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26, versus about 22% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.quote:
Title: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)

CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)

Endpoint | Drug R 10 mg (N=296) | Placebo (N=294) | Difference or OR (95% CI) | p-value
Body weight, kg, LS mean change (SE) | -2.1 (0.3) | -0.6 (0.3) | -1.5 (-2.3, -0.7) | <0.001
Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1) | -15.4 (-21.2, -9.6) | <0.001
HbA1c <7.0%, n (%) | 118 (39.9) | 64 (21.8) | OR 2.41 (1.68, 3.46) | <0.001
result.location: CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2, HbA1c <7.0% row and table heading
result.reason: At week 26, the table reports HbA1c below 7.0% in 39.9% of Drug R 10 mg patients and 21.8% of placebo patients, matching the approximate percentages claimed.

item.claim: Nausea was the most common adverse event with drug R, reported by 12.0% of patients versus 4.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.quote:
Preferred term | Drug R 10 mg (N=300) n (%) | Placebo (N=298) n (%)

Diarrhoea | 24 (8.0) | 15 (5.0)
Urinary tract infection | 15 (5.0) | 14 (4.7)

result.reason: Nausea has the highest reported incidence for Drug R in the table, at 12.0%, compared with 4.0% for placebo.

item.claim: Drug R reduced HbA1c significantly more than placebo at every visit through week 52.
item.label: supported

result.reason: At every visit reported through week 52, Drug R had a greater HbA1c reduction than placebo, with p<0.001.

item.claim: Hypoglycaemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) was reported in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL in 4.0% of Drug R patients and 1.0% of placebo patients.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction appeared smaller in patients with eGFR below 60 (difference -0.38%) than in those with eGFR of 60 or above (-0.72%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports a smaller treatment difference in HbA1c change for eGFR <60 (-0.38%) than for eGFR ≥60 (-0.72%).

item.claim: The treatment effect on HbA1c was consistent across age subgroups (interaction p = 0.61).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an age-subgroup interaction p-value of 0.61, consistent with no detected difference in treatment effect between the age subgroups.

item.claim: Shifts in ALT to more than three times the upper limit of normal were rare (0.7% on drug R, 0.3% on placebo).
item.label: supported

result.quote:
Parameter | Drug R 10 mg (N=300) mean change (SD) | Placebo (N=298) mean change (SD) | Shift to >3x ULN, n (%) R / P
ALT, U/L | +1.8 (9.4) | +0.9 (8.7) | 2 (0.7) / 1 (0.3)
result.reason: The table reports ALT shifts to >3× ULN in 0.7% of drug R recipients and 0.3% of placebo recipients.

item.claim: Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups; mean age was 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c 8.3% and 8.2%.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The reported mean ages and HbA1c values match the claim, and the listed baseline characteristics are similar between groups.

item.claim: Fasting plasma glucose fell by 24.3 mg/dL on drug R versus 8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1) | -15.4 (-21.2, -9.6) | <0.001
result.location: CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2, fasting plasma glucose row
result.reason: The week 26 table reports fasting plasma glucose decreases of 24.3 mg/dL with Drug R and 8.9 mg/dL with placebo.

item.claim: One patient on drug R and two on placebo died during the study.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports one death in the Drug R group and two in the placebo group.

item.claim: Drug R was well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: drug-related 24.0 vs 13.8, discontinuation 6.0 vs 2.3, grade>=3 9.0 vs 6.0

result.quote:
Drug-related TEAE | 72 (24.0) | 41 (13.8)
TEAE leading to discontinuation | 18 (6.0) | 7 (2.3)
result.reason: Drug-related adverse events and discontinuations were more frequent with Drug R than with placebo, so the table does not substantiate a similar adverse event profile.

item.claim: Drug R did not increase the risk of hypoglycaemia.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Hypoglycaemia was reported in 4.0% of Drug R patients versus 1.0% of placebo patients, contrary to the claim.

item.claim: Gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: severity and duration aren't in the table

result.reason: The table reports how often these gastrointestinal events occurred, but not their severity or duration.

item.claim: No safety signals were identified for hepatic or renal function.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: eGFR fell 2.9 vs 1.1; 'no signal' is a conclusion the table can't make

result.reason: The table reports ALT elevations above 3x ULN and a greater mean eGFR decline with Drug R than placebo, so it does not establish that no hepatic or renal safety signals were identified.

item.claim: The HbA1c benefit of drug R was consistent across renal function subgroups.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The treatment effect differs between renal function subgroups, with a significant interaction (p=0.04), so the table does not support a consistent benefit.

item.claim: Drug R is safe in patients with renal impairment.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: CSR-DRX201, Table 14.3.1: Overview of treatment-emergent adverse events (safety population)
result.reason: The table reports adverse events for the overall safety population, not for patients with renal impairment, so it does not establish safety in that subgroup.

item.claim: Older patients (65 years and above) derived a significantly smaller benefit than younger patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Although the estimated benefit is numerically smaller in patients aged 65 years and above, the interaction p-value of 0.61 does not support a significant difference by age.

item.claim: In patients with eGFR below 60, drug R significantly reduced HbA1c versus placebo (difference -0.38%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The reported difference is -0.38%, but its 95% confidence interval includes zero, so the table does not support a statistically significant reduction.

item.claim: In the safety population, HbA1c fell by 0.94% at week 26.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote:
CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.1: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) by visit (full analysis set, MMRM)

Week 26, LS mean change (SE) | -0.94 (0.06) | -0.28 (0.06) | -0.66 (-0.83, -0.49) | <0.001
result.reason: The −0.94% week-26 change is reported for the full analysis set, not the safety population.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased steadily through week 52.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The HbA1c reduction with Drug R was smaller at week 52 (−0.81%) than at week 26 (−0.94%), so it did not increase steadily through week 52.

item.claim: Weight loss with drug R was driven by its gastrointestinal effects.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports weight loss but does not establish that gastrointestinal effects drove it.

item.claim: At week 52, drug R reduced body weight by 2.1 kg.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote:
Title: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)

CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)

Endpoint | Drug R 10 mg (N=296) | Placebo (N=294) | Difference or OR (95% CI) | p-value
Body weight, kg, LS mean change (SE) | -2.1 (0.3) | -0.6 (0.3) | -1.5 (-2.3, -0.7) | <0.001
result.reason: The table reports a 2.1 kg body-weight reduction for Drug R at week 26, not week 52.

item.claim: The maximal HbA1c reduction was reached by week 12.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The Drug R HbA1c reduction was greater at week 26 than at week 12, so the maximum had not been reached by week 12.

item.claim: Drug R also lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The point estimate favors Drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant, so the table does not establish that Drug R lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.

item.claim: Headache was more common with drug R than with placebo (3.7% vs 4.4%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The percentages match, but headache was less common with Drug R than with placebo (3.7% vs 4.4%), not more common.

item.claim: Drug R tripled the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c below 7.0%.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The proportion was 39.9% with Drug R versus 21.8% with placebo, not three times as high.

item.claim: Any adverse event was reported by 57.0% of drug R patients and 61.0% of placebo patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The claim reverses the groups: 61.0% of Drug R patients and 57.0% of placebo patients reported a treatment-emergent adverse event.

item.claim: Drug R caused urinary tract infections in 5.0% of patients.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: 5.0 vs 4.7 on placebo; incidence isn't causation

result.reason: The table reports urinary tract infections in 5.0% of Drug R patients but does not establish that Drug R caused them.

item.claim: eGFR increased slightly with drug R over 52 weeks.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Drug R's mean eGFR change from baseline to week 52 was −2.9 mL/min/1.73m2, indicating a decrease rather than an increase.

item.claim: Drug R provides an additional blood pressure benefit of 1.3 mmHg.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The estimated additional reduction is 1.3 mmHg, but the confidence interval includes no benefit and the difference is not statistically significant, so the table does not establish a blood pressure benefit.

item.claim: Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 50% more frequent with drug R (9.0% vs 6.0%), all of them drug-related.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: relatedness of grade 3 events not in table

result.quote:
Drug-related TEAE | 72 (24.0) | 41 (13.8)
Grade 3 or higher TEAE | 27 (9.0) | 18 (6.0)
result.reason: The table supports the 9.0% versus 6.0% comparison but does not establish that all grade 3 or higher events were drug-related.

item.claim: Haematocrit decreased with drug R.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports a mean haematocrit increase of 1.9% from baseline to week 52 with Drug R, not a decrease.
